source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 13ης Μαρτίου — «Άγιος Πούπλιος, Ιερομάρτυρας Επίσκοπος Αθηνών»

attestations.note: The page makes him bishop of Athens after the holy Narcissus, in the second century, and puts his martyr's death in the persecution of Marcus Aurelius «(161-180 μ.Χ.)». It prints two lines of verse and no hymn. The Greek calendar keeps a second Publius on this same day, the martyr of the trio with Africanus and Terentius, who is another man.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 26.03.2026 (13. март ст. ст.) — „Свештеномученик Публије.“

attestations.note: The day's third and last entry, read as this bishop and not as the other Publius the Greek keeps on this same day: the Prologue makes him a bishop at Athens in the second century, killed by unbelievers, which is what saint.gr makes this folder, while the Publius of the trio with Africanus and Terentius is a lay martyr with companions and the Prologue names no companions here. The two pages disagree over whose see he took: the Prologue makes him successor in the episcopate of the glorious Dionysius the Areopagite, where saint.gr puts him next after the holy Narcissus. The disagreement is recorded and neither reading is preferred; the identification does not rest on it, since both make him the second-century bishop of Athens. The Prologue adds the manner of death saint.gr withheld — he was beheaded — and dates him only to the second century, which is wider than the reign of Marcus Aurelius this folder already holds from saint.gr, so the sourced interval is not widened. The stored Serbian form is the bare forename: the heading gives the rank word Свештеномученик and nothing else, no see and no epithet, so it folds with `publius-of-zeugma`, which holds the same bare form off its own Julian 25 January heading, and that fold is recorded as deliberate. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

death.note: saint.gr: «τελείωσε αυτή με μαρτυρικό θάνατο κατά τον διωγμό του αυτοκράτορα Μάρκου Αυρηλίου (161-180 μ.Χ.)», and it puts him «κατά τον δεύτερο αιώνα μετά Χριστόν». The page gives no year, so the interval is the reign it prints.
